breadboard.port_rule: Holes are named '<column><bank>.<row>': column 1-30, bank 't' (top half, rows a-e) or 'b' (bottom half, rows f-j), e.g. '12t.c', '7b.h'. The 5 holes of one column-bank are one strip. Power rails: 'tp.<n>', 'tn.<n>', 'bp.<n>', 'bn.<n>' (each rail is one strip).

buzzer.note: Polarised piezo buzzer: pin 2 is + (goes to the signal pin, e.g. the Arduino pin), pin 1 is - (goes to GND). Do not reverse it.

led-matrix-8x8.note: 1088AS/788BS-style 8x8 matrix, pins numbered 1-16 counter-clockwise from the bottom-left (printed side down): rows R1-R8 are pins 9, 14, 8, 12, 1, 7, 2, 5; columns C1-C8 are pins 13, 3, 4, 10, 6, 11, 15, 16. Rows are the LED anodes, columns the cathodes. Wire a board pin to the matrix PIN the tutorial names, then find which row/column that pin is.

midi-jack.note: 5-pin DIN socket, pins numbered 1-5 as printed (1 and 3 unused). MIDI out from a board: pin 4 to +5V through a 220 ohm resistor, pin 5 to the TX pin through a 220 ohm resistor, pin 2 to ground.

pushbutton.note: 4 legs in two pairs: 1.l and 1.r are ALWAYS joined inside (side 1), 2.l and 2.r are ALWAYS joined (side 2); pressing joins side 1 to side 2. Wire the input pin to one side and the supply to the OTHER side; a pull-down/pull-up resistor goes on the SAME side as the input pin.

rgb-led.note: Common-anode or common-cathode RGB LED: the long common leg is COM; R, G and B each need their own resistor.
